business_problem: AT&T needed a way for teams to automate time-consuming customer service and network-operations tasks across multiple internal systems while keeping humans in control and maintaining privacy, security, and faster response for customers.
solution_summary: AT&T uses Ask AT&T Workflows, an internal extension of its Ask AT&T platform, to let employees design multi-agent workflows through a graphical drag-and-drop builder instead of coding each automation from scratch. In the first production deployment, AT&T Business and technology development teams configured agents to accept customer service update requests, synchronize data across internal systems, and auto-install information in real time, with humans overseeing required checkpoints. For retrieval and context, the agents pull enterprise information from Ask Docs and Ask Data, AT&T’s proprietary GenAI tools that securely house company knowledge and data. The same pattern is applied to network operations: agents ingest alerts and telemetry, correlate issue location, retrieve recent change logs and known-issue records, open trouble tickets, propose remediations, and assemble resolution artifacts for engineer review. Logging, data isolation, retention policies, and role-based access govern each handoff between agents.

solution_components.name: Ask AT&T Workflows
solution_components.role: Provides the graphical builder and orchestration layer employees use to create and run multi-agent workflows for customer service and network operations.

solution_components.name: Ask Docs
solution_components.role: Supplies securely housed AT&T information that agents retrieve to inform decisions and actions.

solution_components.name: Ask Data
solution_components.role: Supplies securely housed AT&T data that agents query during workflow execution for informed actions.

data_flow: Employee-built agents created in Ask AT&T Workflows ingest customer service requests or network alerts, pull enterprise context from Ask Docs and Ask Data plus telemetry, change logs, and known-issue records, then coordinate actions such as synchronizing records, auto-installing information, opening trouble tickets, proposing fixes, and compiling summaries for human review.
business_outcome: AT&T reports that the first production workflow is delivering value at scale by improving customer experience, reducing wait times, helping employees focus on higher-priority work, and enabling faster response to network incidents.
architecture_clues: A human oversees the chain of agents and required checkpoints throughout execution.
Agents operate within AT&T's ecosystem and can hand work from one agent to the next.
Every action taken by the agents is logged.
Data isolation, retention policies, and role-based access are enforced across agent handoffs.
Network-operations agents can correlate telemetry, inspect change logs and known issues, open tickets, draft code patches, and compile post-incident artifacts.
